issue_context.title: Scheduler policy api compatibility test should apply feature gates
issue_context.body:
Currently it does not, and that is not correct, it caused an accidental break in our compatibility since ```TaintNodesByCondition``` graduated to Beta: we removed the registration of "CheckNodeMemoryPressure, CheckNodePIDPressure, CheckNodeDiskPressure, CheckNodeCondition", but the compatibility test didn't catch that.

/sig scheduling
/help
/priority important-soon
comments:
@notpad One tip to reuse the snippet when applying featuregates in tests:

```go
defer algorithmprovider.ApplyFeatureGates()()
```

So that each unit test (or subtest) is atomic.

review_comments:
A more straightforward solution is to add a parameter with type `func()` to the original "schedulerFiles" - which can be renamed to "testcases".
And also the struct `map[string]struct` can be refactored to `[]struct`, and add a field called "name" into the anonymous struct - which then follows the Golang subtest convention.

In terms of the new `func()` field, the subtest can choose to implement as a no-op or apply specific alpha/beta featuregate, and inside the main test body (the `for ... range testcases` loop), we call the `func()` in the beginning, and then call `defer algorithmprovider.ApplyFeatureGates()()`.

Thanks @Huang-Wei. Yes, this will make the tests to follow the Golang subtest convention. My previous solution intends to apply the alpha/beta featuregate to all of the tests from 1.0 to 1.16, so this is not needed and we just need to add two alpha/beta featuregate examples based on 1.16, right?
